title: Deep Work, lesson 1: focus is rare and valuable

slides.head: Its value keeps *climbing*. Fewer people can do it.
slides.body: The more the world distracts us, the more a focused mind is worth.

slides.head: Most of us are *interrupted* all day.
slides.body: Pings, tabs and inboxes chop the day into fragments.

slides.head: Every switch leaves part of you *behind*.
slides.body: Researcher Sophie Leroy calls it *attention residue*: part of your mind stays on the last task.

slides.head: Even a quick inbox check leaves a *fog*.
slides.body: Your focus takes a while to climb back.

slides.head: One focused hour can *beat* several distracted ones.
The focus *formula*
slides.body: Cal Newport's idea in one line.

slides.head: Deep focus *in action*
slides.body: Jason Benn changed careers through deep, undistracted study.

slides.head: That gap is your career *opportunity*.
slides.body: Few people can focus deeply. Be one of them.
